title: UC San Diego Resting State EEG Data from Patients with Parkinson's Disease
description: This dataset comprises resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) recordings collected from patients with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls at the University of San Diego. The study includes 31 participants with recordings acquired both on and off dopaminergic medication for patient groups, enabling investigation of medication effects on cortical oscillatory dynamics. The dataset supports research into the neurophysiological signatures of Parkinson's disease, including alterations in beta-band synchronization and cortical activity patterns.
methods_description: Resting-state EEG recordings were collected using BioSemi acquisition systems. Healthy control participants completed a single recording session, while Parkinson's disease patients underwent two sessions: one on dopaminergic medication and one off medication. UPDRS rating scales were administered by laboratory personnel trained through online certification rather than board-certified neurologists. Cognitive screening included MMSE assessment.
